# [CS005] Cross-Site Scripting (xss)

Untrusted data is written into an HTML response without escaping.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html) |
| **OWASP** | A05:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Writing request data to a ResponseWriter, or converting it to template.HTML, lets an attacker inject script that runs with the victim's session. html/template escapes values according to their context; text/template and fmt do not.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func hello(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	fmt.Fprintf(w, "<h1>Hello %s</h1>", r.URL.Query().Get("name"))
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
var page = template.Must(template.New("p").Parse("<h1>Hello {{.}}</h1>"))

func hello(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	_ = page.Execute(w, r.URL.Query().Get("name"))
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [xss]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    xss: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore xss -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** xss
```
